On Mon, 2014-07-28 at 10:27 -0700, Michael T wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I'm looking at the example code from
> http://www.r-inla.org/examples/case-studies/blangiardo-et-al-2012
> and trying to adapt it to my toy example.
>
> My implementation runs, however I skipped two steps, and i'm wondering
> if they are important and necessary
>
> Question 1) Having a dataframe and a graph adjacency object, does the
> dataframe need to be sorted the same way as the graph object?

Hi,

you're free to do this as you want, as long as you do it 'right'
according to your model/data. The concept is really simple, and I guess
you're unsure about how this works.

With

formula = y ~ x + f(idx, model="besag", graph=....)

and

data = data.frame(y, x, idx)

then for i=1...nrow(data)

linear.predictor[i] = intercept + beta.x * x[i] +
B[idx[i]]


Here 'B' is the besag-model, which is multivariate Normal with indices
1, 2,..., sizeofthegraph. The contribution to the i'th linear predictor,
is just the idx[i]'th element of B.


As you see, you can order the data.frame as you like, as long as you
keep the internal ordering.

Hope this helps.

H




--
Håvard Rue

Thanks Prof Rue,

it clears it up and I also figured out the easy way to do the sorting for good measure.

data = data.frame(y, x, ids,idt)

xx <- data
yy <- row.names(AA)

AA is the adjacency matrix

# this orders by date, then by supplied order of row.names(AA)
test <- xx[order(xx$idt,match(xx$ids,yy)),]

resulting in data of the form

for t in 1:T{
  for s in 1:S{

}
}
